title: Effect of an idle action
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $r\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{dec}:\mathbb{N}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, and let $x$ be a finite Boolean input. For any amplified configuration $C$, input-head movement $\mathrm{inp}\in\{-1,0,1\}$, optional Boolean output $\mathrm{out}$, and optional successor phase $\mathrm{st}$, applying the action that makes no changes to work tapes or their head positions, emits $\mathrm{out}$, and sets the state to $\mathrm{st}$ yields the configuration with state $\mathrm{st}$, input-head position moved according to $\mathrm{inp}$, unchanged work tapes and work-tape head positions, and output equal to the prior output followed by $\mathrm{out}$ if present.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
